  "explanation": "The trace shows frame_len=3 vs expected=1 at cycle 5, with tkeep=1 (single byte) on a tlast transfer. The loop counts bits by matching tkeep against left-aligned masks, but tkeep=1 is right-aligned (LSB). For i=0: mask=0 -> no match; i=1: mask=128 -> no match; ... i=8: mask=255 -> no match. bit_cnt stays 0, yet frame_len becomes 3, implying the loop runs three times. The combinational block executes on every valid+ready cycle. At cycle 2 (first data), frame_reg=0 so frame_len_next=0 then +bit_cnt. If bit_cnt=1 (bug), frame_len=1. Cycle 3: frame_reg=1, frame_len=1+bit_cnt. Cycle 4: frame_len=1+2*bit_cnt. Cycle 5 (tlast): frame_len=1+3*bit_cnt=3 -> bit_cnt=1 per cycle. The loop must be matching i=1 incorrectly. candidate_014 adds !tlast to the new-frame condition (!frame_reg && !tlast), preventing new-frame reset on single-cycle frames, but the real issue is the bit counting. However, given the menu, candidate_014 and candidate_004 (gate main condition with !tlast) can suppress counting on tlast cycles. candidate_006 (!frame_reg) on main condition would only count on first cycle. candidate_019 (KEEP_ENABLE && frame_reg) would only count inside frames. candidate_018 (!tvalid) on tlast condition is irrelevant. candidate_022 (KEEP_ENABLE && !tlast) suppresses counting on tlast. candidate_001/002 are state retention/resets."
